summary: Choose the columns a report actually needs.
syntax: SELECT column_a, column_b FROM table_name ORDER BY column_a;
documentation: SELECT evaluates result expressions for the input rows. Listing columns explicitly controls the shape and names of the returned data.
inputs: A source table and the expressions or columns to return.
returns: A result set with the requested columns.
caution: Rows have no guaranteed order without ORDER BY. SELECT * can expose columns a report does not need.
scenarios: Export only the fields another system needs.
Inspect a small table before writing a more complex query.
title: List the order owners
problem: Return id and customer from every order, sorted by id ascending. Include rows with a NULL customer.
goal: Use SELECT or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Select the two named columns and order by id.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT query against the example tables.
SELECT 1;

tests.name: Missing customer
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, NULL, 100, 'paid');
